page: Amazon Web Services r8id.4xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on the AWS Nitro System hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor operating at 3.9 GHz, providing 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 8 physical cores with two threads per core. The hardware architecture incorporates a 480 MB L3 cache, along with Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 vector support. System memory totals 128 GB of high-speed DDR5 running at 7 GHz, delivering an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Attached directly to the instance is 950 GB of high-speed NVMe SSD local instance storage alongside a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps. GPU acceleration is not present on this hardware tier.

Performance benchmarks show balanced multi-threaded compute and elevated single-core throughput. The instance achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 2,176, placing it in the top 25 percent of tested systems, while the multi-core score registers at 13,108. Single-threaded compression operations are strong, reaching 34.26 GB/sec in gzip compression and 14.53 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. In Geekbench text processing, the server scores 2,965, placing in the top 10 percent. Large-block memory bandwidth delivers 115.87 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 65.94 GB/sec for write operations. Leveraging integrated AMX instructions, lightweight language model generation achieves top-tier results at 339.94 tokens per second on 135M parameter models, alongside sustained throughput of 30.14 million operations per second on Redis SET workloads.

From an efficiency standpoint, the r8id.4xlarge balances high-density DDR5 memory and bundled NVMe scratch storage without the architectural overhead or cost of dedicated GPU coprocessors. However, the 8 Gbps baseline network throughput represents a potential bottleneck for distributed clustering tasks requiring massive cross-node replication. The combination of dense DDR5 memory, strong per-core text processing, and integrated NVMe storage makes this instance suited for in-memory databases, Redis caching clusters, real-time analytics pipelines, and I/O-intensive transactional database engines.
description: Amazon Web Services r8id.4xlarge is a memory-optimized Nitro-based virtual server engineered for high memory density and localized storage throughput. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs derived from an 8-core Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor operating at 3.9 GHz, backed by 480 MB of L3 cache, AVX-512, and AMX execution units. Memory capacity stands at 128 GB of DDR5 operating at 7 GHz, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. A 950 GB NVMe SSD provides local ephemeral storage, accompanied by an 8 Gbps baseline networking interface. Benchmark evaluations highlight top-decile text processing and small-scale LLM text generation at 339.94 tokens per second, with strong single-threaded data compression reaching 34.26 GB/sec. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth registers at 115.87 GB/sec. This configuration offers high resource consolidation for in-memory databases, key-value stores like Redis, operational data caching, and transactional database workloads requiring fast local scratch storage.
